prs.title: Editorial: Consolidate typed array initialization from an iterable or array-like
prs.author: gibson042
prs.body: Merge InitializeTypedArrayFromList and InitializeTypedArrayFromArrayLike into a single InitializeTypedArrayFromElements operation, as described at https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/pull/3984#discussion_r4098937394.

prs.title: Layering: use an enum for the compilation type
prs.author: nicolo-ribaudo
prs.body:
Implements https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/pull/3294#discussion_r4039302116, and that PR will need to be rebased on top of this one.

* [HTML Standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/): it just propagates the args as they are without typing them: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#hostensurecancompilestrings(realm,-parameterstrings,-bodystring,-codestring,-compilationtype,-parameterargs,-bodyarg)
* CSP: the function signature is already typed as "an enum" because it already incorporated the dynamic code brand checks proposal (https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#can-compile-strings)

prs.title: Normative: Integrate "dynamic code brand checks" proposal
prs.author: lukewarlow
prs.body:
This change introduces a new HostGetCodeForEval host hook, this is used to allow evaluating certain objects.

This change also provides the compilation type and the original arguments, to the host hook HostEnsureCanCompileStrings.

This PR upstreams ~~a reduced version of~~ the https://github.com/tc39/proposal-dynamic-code-brand-checks proposal

Closes https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/pull/1498, https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/issues/938

> [Nicolò] The first commit is from https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/pull/3998, which @linusg and @gibson042 asked to split into its own PR.

prs.title: Editorial: introduce figures with a description
prs.author: nicolo-ribaudo
prs.body:
https://github.com/tc39/ecmarkup/pull/664 changes the position of figure captions to be below rather than above, meaning that some figures would suddenly appear in the text with no introduction:

This PR ensures that we always start with a paragraph introducing what the figure is about.

prs.title: Editorial: Use OrdinaryObjectCreate in {Async,}DisposableStack.prototype.move()
prs.author: linusg
prs.body: The "prototype" property of %DisposableStack% and %AsyncDisposableStack% is non-writable and non-configurable, so the fallback intrinsic passed to OrdinaryCreateFromConstructor is never used. This matches how the Set methods create their results, for example.
